newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai sugar vessels movement steady this week.
newsitem.headline: Thai sugar vessels movement steady this week.

text.p: Sugar shipment from Thailand continued to be slow this week due to limited market supply ahead of the crushing season, industry sources said on Thursday.
About 65,000 tonnes of white and raw sugar was shipped or expected to be loaded or shipped to various destinations between September 3-20, they said.
The vessel Queen Commandor left the Thai port on September 9 with 9,500 tonnes of bagged white sugar, heading to Indonesia.
Marubeni, Kerry, Tate & Lyle and Phibro were said to be buyers, they said.
Louis Dreyfus was said to be the buyer of 2,000 tonnes of bagged raw sugar which was shipped to Maputo on September 9.
The vessel Akademik Pozdyunin was now loading 3,000 tonnes of bagged white sugar to Pakistan. Cargill was a buyer, the sources said.

Another vessel was expected to arrive for loading 5,000 tonnes of bagged white sugar to be shipped to Dubai between September 13-18. The loading will be cancelled if the ship fails to arrive at the port during the specified period, they said.
